titleEn: Dirty Hands? Down to the Stream!

pages.text: "I want the first bite of that bread!" Ppino the rabbit, always first at everything, hopped out of a burrow. Dirt covered their hands. The smell of bread came from the lodge door, down the slope.
Ppino ran to the long table and grabbed the biggest loaf. Mei the timid baby goat opened wide eyes. "Ppino, your hands are dirty..." "It's fine. I'll eat fast, then go digging again!"
Ppino touched this loaf, then that one. Dark handprints dotted every loaf. Mei quietly set down their bread. "It has handprints..." Mei said softly.
Grandma Bear, who ran the lodge, carried the whole plate into the kitchen. "We'll give these to the birds. Yours was on here too, Ppino." Ppino's tummy rumbled.

Grandma spread Ppino's hands wide. Dark dirt filled every space between the fingers. "Dirty hands? Down to the stream!" Grandma pointed to the stream below the door. Ppino turned their hands over and blinked.
The stream water was cold. Ppino dipped both hands in. Grandma placed white soap in their palm. "Rub between your fingers too." She rubbed her own hands to show them.
Ppino swished their hands in the water. Dark water flowed downstream, revealing clean pale palms. "Dirty hands? Down to the stream!" Ppino shook their wet hands and smiled.
Grandma offered Ppino one loaf she had saved. Ppino took it in both hands, and the bread stayed white. Their ears leaned forward. "Not a single mark!"
The next morning, Ppino stopped digging the burrow and dipped both hands in the stream. "One, into the water! Two, rub with soap! Three, swish and rinse!" Their palms were soon clean.
Grandma sat Ppino on her lap and hugged them warmly. Pick up bread with washed hands, and it stays white. "Dirty hands? Down to the stream!" Ppino took a big bite of white bread.
